summary: Declare mission-only per-person attention budgets as ordered data, without budget counting, comparison, admission or enforcement

replay.detail: No receipt, replay or historical interpretation changes; declarations extend existing mission data only.

schema.detail: No database tables, indexes, migrations or claim kinds change. Empty attention arrays are omitted, preserving old declarations' canonical bytes and hashes.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rules change. Attention declarations describe a rolling seven-day, per-person contract including delegated descendants and every declaring ancestor; no counting, comparison, admission or enforcement is added, and existing local attention reporting is unchanged.

compatibility.detail: KDL and typed mission budgets gain strict ordered attention entries with person and asks; unknown budget members still refuse. All new declared-admission publication continues to require features.declared_admission=1 from every active incarnation, including the local daemon. Publications containing attention additionally require features.declared_attention=1 from every active incarnation. Both capabilities use each incarnation's latest signed, authenticated, own-origin daemon.started advertisement anchored to the admitted incarnation. Missing or unsupported capability evidence refuses before writes with declared-admission-feature-barrier. Attention-free declarations continue publishing in mixed fleets with version-1 declared-admission support. Semantic validation retains invalid-declared-admission. Mixed-version execution was not exercised for this change.

downtime.detail: No migration or additional downtime mechanism; daemon upgrades require the usual restart. Restart duration was not measured.

manual.detail: Before publishing attention, upgrade every active member to advertise features.declared_attention=1 or fence old peers, and wait for the latest signed, authenticated, anchored own-origin advertisements. Keep features.declared_admission=1 for all declared-admission publications. Attention-free declarations can continue publishing in mixed fleets with version-1 declared-admission support. Keep supporting readers while attention metadata is active.

recovery.detail: Remove attention metadata using supporting binaries before a mixed-version rollback to readers that reject it. Attention-free declarations remain publishable with features.declared_admission=1 support throughout the active fleet; publishing attention additionally requires features.declared_attention=1. Upgrade or fence incompatible members to publish attention; no database rollback or replay is required.
